audits.dominantPattern: contrast pivot / chained negation where the positive half already carries the fact

findings.text: through the gates instead of over them and into the dark
findings.pattern: NEG-P1 inverted contrast pivot (Y instead of X)
findings.deletionTest: A great many of them had gone out on their own feet, empty-handed and at a walk, through the gates and into the dark.
findings.reason: Pattern 1. Nobody in the scene climbed or could have climbed 'over' the gates, so the rejected option is not a real alternative; the flattened gate at L233 already carries the image.
findings.suggestedFix: straight through the gates and into the dark

findings.text: "Nothing turned off, either. There's a gap in the bank back there, a track down to a farm. Not one of them went into it. And none came back down. Every mark in this cut goes the one way."
findings.pattern: NEG-P7 chained negation building to a positive summary
findings.deletionTest: "There's a gap in the bank back there, a track down to a farm. Every mark in this cut goes the one way."
findings.reason: Pattern 7. Three refusals ('Nothing turned off' / 'Not one of them went into it' / 'none came back down') lead up to 'Every mark in this cut goes the one way', and that last line already holds all three facts. 'Nothing turned off' and 'Not one of them went into it' repeat the same check. The deletion test survives, so the dialogue defense does not apply.
findings.suggestedFix: "There's a gap in the bank back there, a track down to a farm. They went past it, every one. Every mark in this cut points uphill."
findings.fixNote: Replace only the quoted speech that follows 'Cyndia's voice went lower, and more careful.' Keep the opening "At least." 'points uphill' is literal toe direction, the same usage as L546 'the toes in the slot pointed north', so it is not intent smear. Cyndia still reports both checks: the farm track and the absence of any returning prints.

findings.text: At noon they watered at a ford that was not the ford, a little gravel crossing where a stream came down under the road.
findings.deletionTest: At noon they watered at a little gravel crossing where a stream came down under the road.
findings.reason: Pattern 4. The sentence names a ford and then takes the name back. The positive half ('a little gravel crossing where a stream came down under the road') already shows this is not the willow-lined river ford from L804, so cutting the negation loses nothing.
findings.suggestedFix: At noon they watered at a little gravel crossing where a stream came down under the road.

No intent, command, judgment, deception or knowledge verb sits on an inanimate subject anywhere in the chapter, and the body-part subjects are all involuntary, observed motion, or a precise physical grip.

Body-part subjects are involuntary (fatigue, flinch, nodding off, the dead foot that never lifts), which is the guide's Pattern 8 exception, or they are the observed motion of a hidden child.
